articles.title: Badshah shares emotional reel after ex-wife Isha Rikhi’s eviction from 'Bigg Boss 20', rapper says, ‘I’m not well, but I love you’
articles.summary: Rapper Badshah has shared an emotional Instagram reel thanking his fans for their love and support, shortly after his ex-wife, Punjabi actress Isha Rikhi,
articles.body: Rapper Badshah has shared an emotional Instagram reel thanking his fans for their love and support, shortly after his ex-wife, Punjabi actress Isha Rikhi, was evicted from the reality show house. In the video, the rapper can be heard speaking in a noticeably strained, low voice, explaining that he is unwell. The post has since gone viral, with fans expressing concern as well as support in the comments.Badshah thanks fans after Isha Rikhi’s exitTaking to Instagram shortly after Isha Rikhi’s eviction, Badshah shared a brief video message for his followers. Speaking in a strained voice, which he attributed to a bad throat, the rapper said, “Hello, kaise ho aap sab log? I just want to thank you for all the love, blessings, and the support. That’s it. Just taking this moment to show my gratitude to all of you.”Apologising for his voice, Badshah added, “I’m not well. But I love you.”The timing of the post comes shortly after Isha’s exit from the reality show, amid renewed public interest in the former couple following their separation earlier this year.Isha Rikhi largely stayed away from discussing BadshahDuring her stint on the show, Isha Rikhi largely refrained from discussing her relationship with Badshah or their brief marriage. Despite entering the house amid considerable curiosity about her personal life, the actress did not extensively discuss their past relationship or make the rapper a central part of her conversations.Her approach surprised some viewers, given the attention surrounding the former couple’s separation.Fans react to Badshah’s emotional videoBadshah’s reel quickly drew reactions from fans, with several users expressing concern over his health and sending him messages of support.One user commented, “Senty hogye bhai aaj,” while another wrote, “Aree bhai esa mat karo, main aap ko spot karuga.” A third comment read, “Bhai koi galat kadam mat uthana.”While some comments focused on supporting the rapper, others appeared concerned about the emotional tone of the video. Badshah himself did not explicitly link the reel to Isha’s eviction or comment on the reasons behind posting the message.Badshah had earlier shared and deleted a reaction to Isha’s evictionBefore sharing the reel, Badshah had posted an Instagram Story reacting to Salman Khan announcing Isha Rikhi’s eviction during the ‘Weekend Ka Vaar’ segment.In the now-deleted story, Badshah appeared to laugh as Salman joked about Isha’s confidence. The rapper subsequently removed the post from his Instagram account.A look at Badshah and Isha Rikhi’s relationshipBadshah and Isha Rikhi reportedly dated for nearly four years before getting married in March 2026. However, just five months after their wedding, the couple announced their separation in August.Both Badshah and Isha shared identical statements on Instagram Stories, confirming that they had mutually decided to part ways and move forward separately. They also requested fans and the media to respect their privacy.Their separation announcement came just months after their wedding and sparked considerable interest among fans, particularly because the couple had largely kept their relationship private.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Tallulah Willis shares rare glimpse of dad Bruce Willis in touching new photo
articles.summary: The sweet father-daughter moment comes weeks after Tallulah Willis' wedding.
articles.body:
Bruce Willis is sharing a sweet father-daughter moment with Tallulah Willis .

Tallulah Willis shared a rare new photo with her father on Instagram on Monday, showing her kissing the actor on the forehead while gently holding his head.

"So cute! 😚😚," the 32-year-old captioned the photo.

Tallulah is the youngest of Bruce Willis and Demi Moore's three daughters.

The touching photo comes weeks after Tallulah married Justin Acee on Aug. 8 at her family's home in Idaho, with her father by her side for the celebration.

Photos from the wedding showed Tallulah resting her head on her father's shoulder as he wrapped an arm around her, while Acee stood beside them holding Bruce Willis' hand.

Bruce Willis' family announced in March 2022 that he had been diagnosed with aphasia and would be stepping away from acting. In February 2023, his family announced that he had received a more specific diagnosis of frontotemporal dementia, or FTD.

Tallulah has previously opened up about cherishing and documenting her time with her father.

"I find that I'm trying to document, to build a record for the day when he isn't there to remind me of him and of us," she wrote in a 2023 essay for Vogue .

She has also shared other glimpses of their bond on social media.

In June 2025, Tallulah posted photos showing her holding her father's hand and embracing him during a family visit.

Earlier that month, she also shared a sweet photo of herself sitting on the floor and hugging Bruce Willis' legs as he sat on a couch.

articles.title: Curta Novo Atendimento: filme de Santos ganha 7 prêmios internacionais | G1
articles.standfirst: 'Novo Atendimento' acompanha a tentativa de um homem de pedir um simples café expresso e usa humor para abordar as dificuldades de serviços cotidianos na era da tecnologia.
articles.summary: O curta Novo Atendimento, de Tales Ordakji, usa o humor para criticar a tecnologia e representa o cinema de Santos no festival FESTin, em Portugal.
articles.body:
Curta-metragem de Santos (SP) participa do FESTin, em Lisboa, Portugal. — Foto: Divulgação

O curta-metragem 'Novo Atendimento', dirigido e estrelado pelo santista Tales Ordakji, foi selecionado para a competição oficial do 17º Festival de Cinema Itinerante da Língua Portuguesa (FESTin), em Lisboa, Portugal. A produção, que já conquistou sete prêmios em festivais no Brasil e no exterior, será exibida no evento realizado entre 1º e 11 de outubro.

Ambientado em Santos , no litoral de São Paulo, o filme de 12 minutos acompanha Lipe, personagem interpretado por Tales, durante uma tentativa de pedir um simples café expresso.

De acordo com a divulgação, o curta mistura comédia e crítica para abordar a dificuldade de realizar serviços do cotidiano na era da tecnologia. Além de Tales, o elenco conta com Cris Eifler e Cibele Gonçalves, que também assina a produção.

A participação no FESTin marca a estreia de “Novo Atendimento” em Portugal. Cibele e Tales viajam ao país a convite do festival, realizado entre 1º e 11 de outubro.

Para Tales, a seleção amplia a circulação internacional da obra e dá visibilidade ao audiovisual produzido na Baixada Santista.

O filme foi produzido pela Atado no Ato com recursos da Lei Paulo Gustavo, do Ministério da Cultura, por meio da Secretaria de Cultura de Santos, com apoio da prefeitura. A produção também teve suporte dos espaços culturais Casa UmMeiaZero, DesenheiTudo e Empreender na Cozinha.

Cibele Gonçalves e Tales Ordakji (à esq.); Cris Eifler e Tales Ordakji (à dir.). — Foto: Divulgação

Desde a estreia, o curta-metragem conquistou sete prêmios em cinco países e foi selecionado para mais de 20 festivais de cinema. Confira as conquistas:

No Brasil: Melhor Filme – Mostra Pega Leve, no Festival de Cinema de Caruaru (PE); Troféu Toninho Dantas, na 17ª Mostra MABS, do Movimento Audiovisual da Baixada Santista.

No exterior: Melhor Curta e Melhor Direção – Oklahoma Latin American Film Festival, nos Estados Unidos; Melhor Ator, para Tales Ordakji – COLIFFE (Coliseum International Film Festival), na Itália; Melhor Curta de Comédia – 9º Digital Griffix Film Awards, no Canadá; Menção Honrosa – London Worldwide Comedy Short, na Inglaterra.

O ator Tales Ordakji contou ao podcast Baixada em Pauta que a carreira começou após o incentivo de um professor em uma aula de artes. A partir dali, procurou cursos de teatro em Santos e seguiu na profissão. Na ocasião, ele afirmou que estava "vivendo um sonho".

articles.title: 'Pralay: Kalyani Priyadarshan shifts to Mumbai for Ranveer Singh starrer, undergoes intense action training, follows special diet ahead of Bollywood debut in Jai Mehta's zombie thriller
articles.summary: Kalyani Priyadarshan has reportedly moved to Mumbai to focus on Pralay, her first Hindi film, in which she stars opposite Ranveer Singh.
articles.body: Kalyani Priyadarshan has reportedly moved to Mumbai to focus on Pralay, her first Hindi film, in which she stars opposite Ranveer Singh. According to a recent report, the 'Lokah' actor has rented an apartment in Juhu and has been preparing extensively for Jai Mehta’s zombie thriller. Kalyani has undergone action training, followed a specialised diet and participated in readings and rehearsals with Ranveer. The film’s next schedule is expected to resume in October.Kalyani Priyadarshan shifts to Mumbai for Pralay prepAccording to a report by Mid-Day, Kalyani Priyadarshan has been based in Mumbai as she prepares for 'Pralay', her upcoming Hindi-language debut. The actor, who has largely been associated with Chennai and Kochi, has reportedly rented an apartment in Juhu to remain close to the film’s preparation and production requirements.A source cited by the publication said the arrangement has been made to allow Kalyani to stay focused on the project until filming is completed. The actor is expected to remain in Mumbai through the production of the film.Kalyani undergoes action training for Ranveer Singh starrer'Pralay' is reportedly demanding an extensive physical preparation from Kalyani. She began action training in May, ahead of the film going on floors in July, and has also been following a specially planned diet for the role.According to the afore mentioned publication, Kalyani and Ranveer have gone through multiple readings, workshops and rehearsals together. The two actors completed the first schedule before Ranveer took paternity leave. The production is expected to resume in October and continue through December.The physical preparation is particularly important for Kalyani's character, with the actor required to maintain a lean physique for the zombie thriller.Kalyani and Ranveer Singh’s 'Pralay' scheduleDirected by Jai Mehta, 'Pralay' is being mounted as a zombie thriller with Ranveer Singh and Kalyani Priyadarshan in the lead. The project marks Kalyani’s entry into Hindi cinema after establishing herself through work in the South Indian film industries.The film’s next schedule is expected to begin in October following Ranveer’s paternity break. The shoot is reportedly planned to continue until December, keeping Kalyani occupied in Mumbai for the coming months.Kalyani Priyadarshan also gave fans a glimpse into her Mumbai schedule through Instagram, revealing that she was “fully locked in to Pralay” this Onam. The actor said she missed celebrating the festival with her family, including the traditional Onam Sadhya and dressing up in a white saree, as work kept her away from home. Instead, she shared a photo dump featuring moments from the past few months and sent her followers warm wishes for the festival.Kalyani Priyadarshan explores more Hindi and South projectsHer Mumbai move is also allowing Kalyani to explore opportunities beyond Pralay. According to the report by the publication, the actor has been meeting filmmakers in the city as she looks to build a career across both Hindi and South Indian cinema.Kalyani Priyadarshan’s work slateOn the work front, Kalyani Priyadarshan was last seen in 'Odum Kuthira Chaadum Kuthira' starring Fahadh Faasil, Revathi Pillai, Dhyan Sreenivasan, Lal, Vinay Forrt and Suresh Krishna. She was also seen in Dulquer Salmaan backed 'Lokah Chapter 1: Chandra' alongside Naslen, Sandy, Chandu Salim Kumar and Arun Kurian.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Vimal Elaichi case: Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff RESPONDED to FDA notices, reveals Tukaram Mundhe- More details inside
articles.summary: Tukaram Mundhe, Commissioner of the Maharashtra FDA, has confirmed that Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff have each responded to the notices
articles.body: Tukaram Mundhe, Commissioner of the Maharashtra FDA, has confirmed that Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff have each responded to the notices issued over their Vimal Elaichi advertisement. Two of the actors sought a hearing, he revealed, and both have now taken place. The regulator says it will be pursuing the matter further.Tukaram Mundhe on hearings in Vimal Elaichi caseAccording to ANI, Tukaram Mundhe revealed, "Regarding those notices, responses from all three have come. Two of them had asked for a hearing. Their hearing was finished yesterday, and we are proceeding further."Maharashtra FDA's notices over Vimal Pan Masala adThe latest development comes weeks after the Maharashtra FDA served show-cause notices on the three actors for featuring in a pan masala advertisement. The regulator alleges the campaign is a case of surrogate advertising for Vimal Pan Masala, which is banned in the state. Shah Rukh, Ajay and Tiger were asked to clarify their roles as brand endorsers and explain why action shouldn't be taken against them. The authority also demanded endorsement-related records, such as contracts, campaign briefs, payment details and evidence of due diligence.FDA cites Food Safety and Standards Act against endorsersThe regulator relied on Section 24 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the provision covering misleading and deceptive food advertisements. It also cited Section 53, which allows a penalty of up to Rs 10 lakh for those involved in publishing such an advertisement. The FDA maintained that celebrity endorsers can't wash their hands of responsibility by pointing the finger at the manufacturer or advertiser.Tukaram Mundhe on due diligence for endorsersEarlier, Mundhe had noted that advertising norms place accountability on the individual or organisation endorsing a product, and that this includes a duty to carry out due diligence.Ajay Devgn, Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff's Vimal associationFor context, Ajay has been associated with Vimal's campaigns for several years now. Shah Rukh later joined the campaign, while Tiger came on board after Akshay Kumar stepped away from it. Akshay had drawn criticism in 2022 for his association with the brand, after which he apologised, announced that he was withdrawing from the endorsement and said he would donate his fee to a cause.Ajay Devgn and Shah Rukh Khan on celebrity endorsementsMeanwhile, Ajay had earlier defended his association with Vimal, clarifying that he was endorsing elaichi rather than pan masala. Shah Rukh, too, has commented on celebrity endorsements in the past, saying that if a product is considered harmful, its manufacture or sale should be stopped instead of holding actors solely responsible.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: 'Hanuman Ansh' continues to hold steady at the box office as it enters Day 55, with its India net collection now at Rs. 312.38 crore at the end of Day 54.
articles.body: 'Hanuman Ansh' continues to hold steady at the box office as it enters Day 55, with its India net collection now at Rs. 312.38 crore at the end of Day 54. Vishal Chaturvedi's spiritual biopic on Neem Karoli Baba, led by Shobhinaw Satyaa, remains firmly on track to add further milestones even after crossing the Rs. 400 crore worldwide mark, with collections continuing to trickle in steadily nearly two months after release on August 7 in India and September 11 in the overseas markets.Having already weathered several ups and downs across its run, from a whisper-quiet start to sudden late bursts of momentum, the film continues to prove its staying power at the ticket window. With its India net collection already at Rs. 312.58 crore at the beginning of Day 55 live tracking, 'Hanuman Ansh' now has the Rs. 315 crore domestic mark within easy reach over the next couple of days. On the worldwide front, with the global gross already past Rs. 408 crore, the film looks set to inch towards the Rs. 410-415 crore range soon, continuing what has become one of the most durable theatrical runs of the year.'Hanuman Ansh's domestic box office run'Hanuman Ansh' had already crossed Rs. 300 crore in India net by the end of Day 52, following a dramatic climb from its modest Rs. 1.08 crore opening week through a series of blockbuster weeks that peaked at Rs. 90.25 crore in Week 5. After a brief cooling-off period on Day 53 with Rs. 2.35 crore, the film added a further Rs. 3.10 crore on Day 54 across 4,411 shows, taking its cumulative India net to Rs. 312.38 crore and gross collection to Rs. 369.00 crore.‘Hanuman Ansh’ overseas collection and worldwide totalInternational markets have continued to add modest but consistent sums through this stretch of the film's run. Having reached Rs. 38.75 crore in overseas gross by the end of Day 53, the film added another Rs. 0.25 crore on Day 54, taking its cumulative overseas total to Rs. 39 crore. Combined with its domestic numbers, this pushed the worldwide gross to Rs. 408 crore by the close of Day 54.'Hanuman Ansh' Day 55 collection live trackingAs per Sacnilk, 'Hanuman Ansh' is currently running across 2,930 shows on Day 55, having added Rs. 1.07 crore to the tally so far in the day.This takes the film's overall India gross to Rs. 370.17 crore and its India net to Rs. 313.35 crore, with the final Day 55 figure expected once all shows for the day have concluded.Day wise collections for 'Hanuman Ansh'Week 1: Rs. 1.08 croreWeek 2: Rs. 0.40 croreWeek 3: Rs. 10.40 croreWeek 4: Rs. 61.00 croreWeek 5: Rs. 90.25 croreWeek 6: Rs. 80.25 croreWeek 7: Rs. 44.80 croreDay 50: Rs. 3.35 croreDay 51: Rs. 6.50 croreDay 52: Rs. 9.00 croreDay 53: Rs. 2.35 croreDay 54: Rs. 3.10 croreDay 55 [LIVE]: Rs. 1.07 croreTOTAL: Rs. 313.35 croreMore about 'Hanuman Ansh'Written and directed by Vishal Chaturvedi, 'Hanuman Ansh' is a devotional biopic based on the early life and teachings of Neem Karoli Baba, also known as Maharaj Ji, tracing his spiritual journey while exploring faith, devotion, compassion and selfless service.Shobhinaw Satyaa plays Neem Karoli Baba, with Purnima Tiwari portraying his wife, Ram Dulari, alongside Chandan Anand as Dr Ram Nandan Bhosale, Anil Rastogi as Mahantji, Gulshan Pandey as Inspector Dharam Singh and Vihaan Shedge essaying Maharaj Ji in his younger years. articles.title: ‘Prahaar’ trailer launch: Maharashtra CM Fadnavis says film carries MESSAGE, praises Rajkummar Rao and Ujjwal Nikam
articles.summary: At the trailer launch of ‘Prahaar: The Untold Story Of Ujjwal Nikam’ on Tuesday, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis talked about the film's
articles.body: At the trailer launch of ‘Prahaar: The Untold Story Of Ujjwal Nikam’ on Tuesday, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis talked about the film's storyline and commended the team behind it. The trailer was unveiled at Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), a station that was among the places targeted in the 26/11 terror attacks.Devendra Fadnavis thanks makers for 26/11 storyFadnavis initiated by thanking the makers for choosing to tell a story built around the 26/11 attacks and the legal fight that followed. He also had words of appreciation for Rajkummar Rao, who plays veteran public prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam, and said Prahaar isn't just meant to entertain but also carries a message.Speaking about how Ajmal Kasab was dealt with after the 26/11 attacks, Fadnavis remarked, "Perhaps if we wanted, we could have killed Kasab. We could have shot him. But our police and our judicial system very thoughtfully showed the world that India is a state where, at least, we can take action against terrorists." He then lauded Advocate Ujjwal Nikam for his part in the Kasab trial, adding, "And I would especially like to thank Ujjwal Nikam ji because he did not just work to ensure that a terrorist was sentenced to death; he also exposed the design behind it, the conspiracy behind it, before the world."Devendra Fadnavis alleges Pakistan's role in 26/11Fadnavis went on to allege that Pakistan was behind the 26/11 attacks, describing them as "state-sponsored terrorism". He gave Nikam credit for exposing what he called the conspiracy behind the attacks to the world. The Maharashtra CM also touched on how Pakistan is viewed in the context of terrorism, calling it a country that "supports terrorism". He added that he had been able to look into the matter closely, and again commended Nikam for the way he handled the case.Lauding Nikam's way of working, Fadnavis said, "Jis professionalism ke saath, jis shiddat ke saath, jis deshbhakti ke saath Ujjwal Nikam ji ne is poore case ko steer kiya..." In his view, Nikam's efforts drew attention to the sacrifice of the police personnel killed during the attacks. Fadnavis recalled officers such as former Mumbai Anti-Terrorism Squad chief Hemant Karkare, Additional Commissioner of Police Ashok Kamte, senior police inspector Vijay Salaskar and Assistant Sub-Inspector Tukaram Omble, among others, and said justice wouldn't have been served in the same manner without them on the ground.Devendra Fadnavis praises Rajkummar Rao and 'Prahaar' teamThe CM also appreciated the film's cast and crew, especially Rajkummar Rao, stating, "Main Prahaar ka bahut-bahut aabhari hoon... Aur Rajkummar Rao jaise accomplished actor, aur poori team itni accomplished hai." He further said, "Toh main yeh keh sakta hoon ki yeh mere entertainment nahi, ismein ek sandesh hai." The remarks suggested he regards the film as more than just entertainment, one that carries a message.Devendra Fadnavis compares 'Prahaar' with 'Chhaava'Citing ‘Chhaava’ as an example, Fadnavis said cinema can make significant episodes of history, and the lives of those who shaped them, accessible to many more people. In his words, ‘Chhaava’ told the story of Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj, the son of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, while Prahaar brings Ujjwal Nikam's story and the 26/11 case to viewers in a similar way. He concluded with an appeal to watch Prahaar and added that he intends to catch the film himself.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Nani and Srikanth Odela’s action thriller ‘The Paradise’ is on its way to complete its first week on the big screens.
articles.body: Nani and Srikanth Odela’s action thriller ‘The Paradise’ is on its way to complete its first week on the big screens. The film opened to a strong response at the box office and minted more than Rs 75 crore worldwide, including special screenings. However, despite a strong headstart, the film received a mixed response from audiences and its box office collections have declined since the opening weekend.As the film is set to complete its first week, the film’s next challenge is to maintain its theatrical run and attract audiences over the coming days. Although the viewers praised the film’s scale and cinematography, it drew criticism for weak writing, pacing issues, underdeveloped characters and technical inconsistencies.‘The Paradise’ day 7 live collectionsAccording to a report by Sacnilk, ‘The Paradise’ has collected over Rs. 62 lakh over 1,455 shows so far on Wednesday.As per today’s live collection the film’s total India net collections stands at Rs. 102.12 crore and the total India gross collections to Rs. 120.73 crore.‘The Paradise’ has been released in multiple languages. The live figures of the Telugu version suggest that it made Rs 52 lakh with 709 shows and Rs 10 lakh with 746 shows in Hindi version as of now.‘The Paradise’ day 6 overseas numbersSpeaking of the collections overseas, on Tuesday the film made Rs 50 lakh, which brings the total overseas gross collections to Rs 30.50 crore. This brings the worldwide gross collection to Rs 150.50 crore.Currently, the film’s total occupancy stands 11.9%.Looking at the box office collection so far, ‘The Paradise’ marked Nani and Srikanth Odela’s biggest opening making Rs 76.90 crore worldwide including its special screenings a day ahead of official release.Day wise collectionDay 0 (special screening): Rs. 11.60 croreDay 1: Rs. 34.65 croreDay 2: Rs. 14.90 croreDay 3: Rs. 15.25 croreDay 4: Rs. 15.70 croreDay 5: Rs. 5 croreDay 6: Rs. 4.40 croreDay 7: Rs. 62 lakhTOTAL: Rs. 102.12 croreNani and Srikanth Odela reunited after the success of their 2023 film ‘Dasara’.About ‘The Paradise’‘The Paradise’ is set in the slums of 1980s Secunderabad, the film follows a marginalized community facing social discrimination and being denied basic rights. 'The Paradise' is a period action drama directed by Srikanth Odela, with Nani playing Jadal, a man from the marginalised Savari community who is drawn into a violent struggle against an oppressive feudal power structure. The film also stars Kayadu Lohar as Subbalakshmi, Mohan Babu as Shikanja Maalik, Raghav Juyal as Vikram Malik and Sonali Kulkarni as Samakka, with Keerthy Suresh appearing in a cameo.The film received an ‘A’ certificate from the CBFC, with reports noting modifications to violent sequences, dialogue and subtitles during the certification process. The certification was issued ahead of its September 24, 2026 theatrical release.Set in 1980s India, The Paradise centres on the Savari community, whose members face marginalisation, lack of rights and exploitation under a powerful feudal system. articles.title: 'Koffee With Karan' one last time: Karan Johar bids emotional farewell to his talk show, here's when and where you can watch the last season
articles.summary: ‘Koffee With Karan’ is set to bid an emotional farewell to its audience.
articles.body: ‘Koffee With Karan’ is set to bid an emotional farewell to its audience. After more than two decades of celebrity confessions, controversial revelations, rapid-fire answers and memorable conversations, Karan Johar is returning with the ninth and final season of the popular chat show.The makers have now released a special glimpse of the upcoming season, featuring Karan reflecting on the show's long journey and revealing why he feels it is finally time to say goodbye.‘Koffee With Karan’ first premiered in 2004 and has since become one of the most talked-about celebrity chat shows on Indian television and streaming. Over the years, the couch has witnessed friendships, romances, fallouts, candid confessions and several moments that went on to dominate headlines.Speaking about the final season, Karan Johar, Host and Creator of Koffee With Karan, said, "There are some journeys you don't plan to end, you simply know, somewhere deep within you, when it is time to let them go. Koffee With Karan has been an extraordinary part of my life. It has given me friendships, memories, moments of complete madness, a lot of love and, yes, its fair share of controversy!""But through all of it, what has remained constant is the audience. They have laughed with us, debated us, trolled us, celebrated us and, most importantly, kept coming back for another cup. Saying goodbye is emotional, but it also feels right. This final season is my way of raising the mug one last time with gratitude, with love and with everyone who has made Koffee With Karan what it is. So, come have one last cup of Koffee with me. One last time," he added.In the emotional video, Karan looks back at how the show came into existence and recalls discussing his idea of hosting a celebrity chat show with his late father in June 2004. He says, "It was June 2004 when I told my dad that I really wanted to host a talk show. I wanted to host two celebrities or stars and have an informal, candid chat with them. He told me, 'Karan, you are going to call your friends, talk to them, something that you do every day anyway. Who will pay you for that?'"Karan further recalled, "He passed away that same month, actually. On 26 June. The very first day I shot for it was 16 August 2004. And I'm here now, eight seasons later, 22 years later, 161 episodes later. A lot happened. I called lovers. I called friends. I called families. I called lovers who went on to become ex-lovers. Some of them even got married. I put an end to the careers of national icons. I am living with the term 'nepo' even today. Conjecture became a national word. So much happened."Looking back at the show's enduring popularity, he said, "Everywhere I go, fortunately or unfortunately, they always ask me, 'When is the next season of Koffee With Karan?' I wonder why they never ask me, 'When is my next feature film?' But whatever it was, it gave me so much. I reached a point in my life where I realised all good things must come to an end. This will be my very last season of Koffee With Karan."Meanwhile, speculation around the celebrity line-up for Season 9 has already been doing the rounds. Names such as Ahaan Panday and Aneet Padda, along with Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna, have been linked to the upcoming season. However, the makers have kept the guest list under wraps so far. The official line-up will be revealed when ‘Koffee With Karan’ Season 9 premieres on October 14.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Ranvir Shorey hit Pooja Bhatt, so I broke his rib, car's glass,' says Rahul Bhatt as he regrets doing so: 'He was very decent, I did a wrong thing'
articles.summary: Ranvir Shorey and Pooja Bhatt's relationship and subsequent fallout have remained a subject of discussion for years.
articles.body: Ranvir Shorey and Pooja Bhatt's relationship and subsequent fallout have remained a subject of discussion for years. Now, Pooja's younger brother Rahul Bhatt has revisited an incident involving Ranvir Shorey from nearly two decades ago, revealing that he once assaulted the actor while stepping in during an altercation between Ranvir and Pooja. Rahul also admitted that he regrets taking matters into his own hands and praised Ranvir for the way he eventually handled the situation.Rahul recalled the incident and said in an interview with Siddharth Kannan, "There was an altercation between Ranvir Shorey and Pooja Bhatt. They had an argument, after which Ranvir hit her or something like that. I had to step in and, when I did, my response was a bit exaggerated. I broke his car's glass. I broke one of his ribs. I did a wrong thing by taking the law into my own hands. Subsequently, I paid the price for it. I was arrested. Charged."Rahul went on to admit that he regretted his actions. He said, "I regret it. I shouldn't have overreacted. Back in those days, I said I would do it again. But in the case of Ranvir Shorey, I shouldn't have. He was very decent. During the compounding of the offence, he came forward and said, 'Let bygones be bygones.'"Praising Ranvir for not holding on to the incident, Rahul added, "Nobody does something like that. People usually use such situations to extract money, but he didn't. He came and compounded the case, and the FIR was quashed. Until then, I had a criminal case pending. He was very decent in that. I respect him for that. Nobody else would have done it without holding a grudge," concluded Rahul Bhatt.The revelation comes amid renewed discussion around Ranvir's tumultuous relationship with Pooja and the allegations that followed their breakup. Ranvir and Pooja, who were friends before entering a relationship, had a highly publicised split in the early 2000s. Pooja had previously alleged that Ranvir was physically and verbally abusive, particularly when he was under the influence of alcohol. Ranvir has denied the allegations.The actor had also spoken about the fallout with the Bhatt family during his stint on Bigg Boss OTT 3, where he emerged as the second runner-up. Recalling that phase of his life, Ranvir had said, “During the same time, I also encountered the biggest scandal of my life with another actress. As I was unable to cope, my brother asked me to come to the US with him for a while. I pursued a six-month acting course in the US and borrowed money from my brother. After returning from the US, I started shooting for The Great Indian Comedy Show in 2005. At that time, two of my long-shelved films were greenlit for release and hit theatres back-to-back within a week, and my work was loved by audiences. After those films, I finally felt my life was steady as an actor and that I had arrived.”Ranvir later discussed the dispute in an interview with Siddharth Kannan, claiming that he felt his equation with Mahesh Bhatt had been used against him. He said, "At the time we had a conflict, I felt that the respect I had for him, he used that manipulatively. When the fight happened, he told my father, 'OK, we will rest the matter here, whatever the fight happened between the kids.' The next day, he proceeded to print utter lies about me and planted false stories in the media against me, painting me as an alcoholic, abusive person. All lies."When asked whether the dispute was only between him and Pooja, Ranvir said, "Her brother was the one who assaulted me. He (Mahesh Bhatt) could have told these guys not to talk like that. In that sense, I felt he was manipulative towards me. These are all 25-year-old stories. I don't want to get into them now."Ranvir and Pooja dated in the early 2000s and lived together before their relationship ended in a much-publicised breakup around 2002. Ranvir later married actress Konkona Sen Sharma. The couple welcomed their son Haroon in 2011 and separated in 2015. Pooja, meanwhile, married Manish Makhija in 2003, though the two later parted ways.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: First Glastonbury Festival 2027 tickets to go on sale
articles.summary: Glastonbury Festival will take place from 23-27 June 2027 at Worthy Farm in Somerset.
articles.body:
Those hoping to go to Glastonbury Festival 2027 could soon find out their fate as the first set of tickets go on sale.

The event will take place from 23-27 June 2027 at Worthy Farm in Pilton, Somerset, after a fallow year in 2026.

Coach tickets will be available to buy for £408 plus the selected coach fare at 18:00 BST on Thursday, before general admission tickets go on sale at 09:00 on Sunday.

Coaches will depart from 28 locations across the country including from London, Bristol, Bath, Glasgow, Edinburgh, Manchester and Cardiff.

Registration closed on 25 September, and will not reopen until after the October ticket sales.

Once on the other side of the queue, people can buy up to six tickets per transaction after paying a deposit.

Anyone who missed the registration deadline or is not able to buy a ticket on Thursday can have another chance during the spring resale.

articles.title: When the human face becomes a language of memory and identity
articles.summary: What can a face reveal beyond the person it belongs to?
articles.body: What can a face reveal beyond the person it belongs to? That question formed the starting point of HEADS – Every Face Holds a Story, a group exhibition that brought together diverse interpretations of the human face at Shridharani Gallery, Triveni Kala Sangam, New Delhi.Curated by gallerist Amrita Kochhar, the exhibition, which concluded on September 23, brought together works by artists including Anjolie Ela Menon, Arpana Caur, Jatin Das, Jogen Chowdhury, K Laxma Goud, Krishen Khanna, Rameshwar Broota, Sakti Burman, Shipra Bhattacharya, Thota Vaikuntam and Vasundhara Broota, among others.Rather than treating the face simply as a subject for portraiture, the exhibition approached it as a visual language — a space where identity, emotion, memory, thought and experience could take different forms.The works moved across styles and generations. While some artists engaged with recognisable faces and portraiture, others used abstraction, distortion, symbolism and imagination to explore what lies beneath or beyond physical appearance. The resulting collection offered contrasting ways of looking at a subject that is at once universally familiar and deeply personal.Several works created specifically for the exhibition were also presented alongside selected works by established artists, bringing together newer interpretations with artistic practices developed over decades.“The head is perhaps one of the most powerful subjects in art. It carries identity, thought, emotion, memory and experience,” said Kochhar. “With HEADS, we wanted to bring together artists who see this subject in profoundly different ways. Every face holds a story, and every artist reveals a different chapter.”The exhibition also carried a personal significance for Kochhar, being held in memory of her late mother, Dr Manjit Kochhar. A doctor who was associated with medicine, charity and seva, she was remembered through the showcase as an individual whose values extended beyond her profession.By bringing together established masters, senior practitioners and contemporary voices, HEADS turned a familiar artistic subject into a conversation about how faces can hold fragments of personal history, cultural memory and imagination.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Roy K John turns the garden into a landscape of memory
articles.summary: What we see when we first look at a garden can be shaped as much by memory as by what lies before our eyes.
articles.body: What we see when we first look at a garden can be shaped as much by memory as by what lies before our eyes. This idea formed the core of Kerala-based artist Roy K John’s recent works, showcased in his solo exhibition Kani: Garden as First Sight at Bikaner House, New Delhi.Curated by Satyajit Dave, the exhibition, which concluded on September 10, brought together John’s recent paintings and 3D wooden works, exploring the garden as a space of memory, perception and transformation.The title draws from the Kerala tradition of ‘Kani’, the auspicious first sight of beauty, abundance and hope traditionally associated with dawn. John uses this idea to move beyond the conventional landscape, creating gardens that feel less like static views of nature and more like visual thresholds.Drawing on his training in traditional Kerala mural painting, the artist builds orchards, groves and botanical forms through layered compositions, rhythmic lines and saturated colours. Vegetation takes on an architectural quality in his works, with tree trunks resembling columns and leaves functioning almost like screens that reveal and conceal fragments of domestic life and memory.The garden, therefore, becomes more than a backdrop. It becomes a space through which the artist explores how people remember places, objects and experiences, and how familiar natural forms can change when viewed through personal memory.The exhibition also featured John’s recent wooden leaf sculptures, extending his engagement with botanical forms into three dimensions. Their tactile quality brought another dimension to his exploration of nature, while also drawing attention to the abundance and fragility of the natural world.“In Roy K John’s garden, the first sight is never simply what is before the eyes. It is what the eye learns to notice,” reads the curatorial note accompanying the exhibition.John’s practice draws on his formal training in traditional mural painting at the Temple of Arts, Guruvayoor, as well as his education at the Kalabhavan School of Arts, Thrissur. His recent works translate elements of Kerala’s classical mural vocabulary into contemporary explorations of landscape and botanical forms.Through Kani, the artist offered a different way of looking at the garden , not simply as a depiction of nature, but as a meeting point between what is seen, what is remembered and what is imagined.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: El canal Gol dice adiós tras una década dedicada a la información deportiva
articles.standfirst: El cierre de la cadena tendrá lugar este mismo miércoles 30 de septiembre
articles.summary: El cierre de la cadena tendrá lugar este mismo miércoles 30 de septiembre
articles.body: El canal Gol cierra después de una década dedicada a la información deportiva. Mediapro ha decidido dar por finalizadas sus emisiones a partir de este mismo miércoles 30 de septiembre. Replay será el canal que le sustituirá desde este 1 de octubre, y, del mismo modo que su predecesor, seguirá ofreciendo un partido de LaLiga Hypermotion en cada jornada. El nuevo canal de Mediapro mantiene el fútbol como uno de sus elementos principales y contará con la emisión de partidos históricos y ligas europeas, aunque ampliará su abanico. Según Vertele, Replay apostará por una programación cercana al público juvenil, menor de 35 años, con una mayor relevancia del contenido en otras plataformas vinculadas a la nueva cadena, como YouTube y redes sociales. La cuenta de X de Replay, que por ahora hereda el @gol en la plataforma, cuenta con más de medio millón de seguidores. Gol, a la que le quedan horas para cesar su emisión de forma definitiva, nació como Gol Televisión en 2008. Entonces era un canal de pago. Pasó a la TDT en 2016 como Gol, en abierto, y en 2025 se enmarcó en la oferta de canales de Movistar, Orange o Vodafone. Replay recoge ahora su testigo, con una fórmula distinta. Uno de los periodistas de la cadena más populares, Ricardo Rosety, anunció su salida de Mediapro el pasado 18 de septiembre a través de X. "Ayer fue mi último día en Mediapro. El último día de una etapa de más de 16 años en GolT, BeIN Sports, Movistar y GOL. Más de 16 años de viajes, Liga, Champions y Europa League, tres Mundiales… El Golazo, Directo GOL, reportajes, entrevistas y tantas historias que contar", explicó.

articles.title: Former NASCAR Driver Ordered to Pay Woman $850K After Alleged Affair with Her Husband Ended Their Marriage
articles.summary: Jennifer Jo Cobb was sued in 2024 by a woman who claimed the driver had an affair with the woman’s husband
articles.body:
A former NASCAR star has been ordered to pay more than $850,000 to a woman who claimed the driver had an affair with her husband

Tracey Hughes sued driver Jennifer Jo Cobb in North Carolina's Davidson County in 2024, alleging alienation of affection and criminal conversation

She accused Cobb of having an affair with her then-husband, NASCAR spotter Clayton Odie Hughes, in the months leading up to their separation

A former NASCAR star has been ordered to pay more than $850,000 to a woman who claimed the driver's alleged affair with her husband ended her marriage.

In 2024, Tracey Hughes filed a lawsuit against driver Jennifer Jo Cobb in North Carolina's Davidson County, accusing her of having an affair with her then-husband, Clayton Odie Hughes, in the months leading up to their divorce, per Fox affiliate WTVT .

In the complaint, Tracey accused Cobb, 53, of alienation of affection , alleging that she encouraged her husband of 17 years — who has worked as a NASCAR spotter since 2003, per Instagram — to lie about taking trips and helped him hide the relationship, the outlet reported.

The complaint alleged that Cobb "willfully, intentionally and deliberately seduced, enticed and alienated the affections" of Clayton before the couple separated in January 2021, according to CBS affiliate WBTV .

In Tracey's second claim, she claimed the affair "invaded and ended" the "exclusive rights and privileges" of her marriage and "dishonored" the couple's "marital bed," asking the court to award her damages for criminal conversation, a civil tort that lets a spouse sue a third party for having sexual relations with their marital partner, per WTVT.

Tracey sought damages exceeding $25,000 for both claims, as well as punitive damages exceeding $25,000, WBTV reported.

On Thursday, Sept. 24, jurors found Cobb liable for both claims and awarded Tracey $50,000 in damages for "maliciously and wrongfully caus[ing] alienation" and $800,000 for "commit[ting] criminal conversation," as well as nominal punitive damages of $1 for each claim, according to court documents reviewed by PEOPLE.

NASCAR 's official website describes Cobb as the holder of several Camping World Truck Series records, including highest-finishing female driver in overall season points and most starts by a female driver.

She is also a member of the 200-plus mph club and one of only a few women with a top-10 finish at "the highest levels" of the sport. She last raced in the Truck Series in 2024.

PEOPLE reached out to Cobb for comment but did not immediately hear back.

articles.title: Sophia Bush Reveals She and Ashlyn Harris Secretly Married: ‘You’re My Wife’
articles.summary: The actress reveals in her new memoir that she and the former soccer star quietly tied the knot in upstate New York in summer 2025
articles.body:
Sophia Bush and Ashlyn Harris quietly married in an intimate ceremony in upstate New York in summer 2025

Harris' children, Sloane and Ocean, joined the couple for the private celebration, which included picking flowers and roasting marshmallows

Bush opens up about marrying Harris in her forthcoming memoir, And I Will Tell You Mine: Notes from a Life in Progress , out Oct. 27

Sophia Bush and Ashlyn Harris are married!

The actress, 44, reveals in her forthcoming memoir, And I Will Tell You Mine: Notes from a Life in Progress , that she and the former professional soccer player quietly tied the knot in an intimate ceremony in upstate New York in summer 2025.

Bush and Harris, who have been together for three years, were joined by Harris' two children, Sloane and Ocean, for the private celebration, the couple revealed to Vogue in a story published on Wednesday, Sept. 30.

"When you get to this stage in your life, you begin to unpack what's yours and what's always sort of been for everyone else," Bush told the outlet of their decision to keep the milestone intimate.

The One Tree Hill alum reflected on how both she and Harris, 40, have spent much of their adult lives in the public eye — Bush as an actress and Harris as a professional athlete.

"It's such a privilege to be able to perform as an athlete or an actor, but it also comes with certain costs," Bush said.

For their wedding day, however, the pair stripped away the pressures that can come with a large celebration and focused on their family.

"The kids were just running and happy, and we picked flowers from the property and our daughter Sloane was holding them," Harris recalled. "It was so fun for them, because it wasn't this pressure-filled day that's too much for young kids."

Bush said the newlyweds ended the evening roasting marshmallows with their family.

"It was so precious, and zero pressure," she recalled. "I will never forget it, and I think wedding days sometimes aren't like that."

Rather than announcing their marriage publicly afterward, Bush and Harris traveled around the country to tell their loved ones the happy news in person.

Once everyone close to them knew, Bush said she was ready to share their new status with the rest of the world, in part because she was tired of referring to Harris simply as her "partner."

"You're not my partner, you know? You're my wife," Bush told Harris. "And it feels so amazing to say that."

The marriage revelation comes as Bush prepares for the Oct. 27 release of her first memoir, And I Will Tell You Mine: Notes from a Life in Progress , which has been nearly a decade in the making.

"I think I finally had to feel ready to answer the call," Bush previously told PEOPLE of writing the book. "I've had my lovely book agent who has the patience of a saint and a handful of editors asking me to write a book for a decade. And for nine years, I said no."

"I think when your life finally feels like all the pieces are in the right place, you start to realize why people might want you to share your story," she added.

In an excerpt from the memoir published by Vogue , Bush reflects on why she and Harris decided to keep their wedding to themselves at first, writing that after years of having so much of her personal life publicly scrutinized, she wanted the milestone to belong to them before sharing it with the world.

Bush also writes about finding inspiration in the decades-long marriage of Harris' grandparents and realizing that Harris was the person with whom she wanted to build her own life.

The actress also reflects on her willingness to embrace marriage again despite knowing firsthand that relationships can end. Bush was previously married to Chad Michael Murray from 2005 to 2006 and Grant Hughes from 2022 to 2024.

Bush and Harris were first linked in October 2023. Bush publicly came out as queer and confirmed their relationship in a 2024 Glamour cover story.

Speaking to Vogue about their decision to share their relationship and marriage publicly, Harris said visibility remained important to them.

"This conversation is not about Sophia and I. We know the love we share," Harris said, adding that "the visibility piece matters" for young people who may not yet feel seen.

Bush and Harris both serve on the board of the Human Rights Campaign and have been active supporters of LGBTQ+ causes.

And I Will Tell You Mine: Notes from a Life in Progress will be released on Oct. 27 and is available now for preorder wherever books are sold.

articles.title: El vino de 200 años que pidió Shakira en su día libre en Madrid: “Pura ensoñación”
articles.standfirst: La intérprete colombiana estuvo en uno de los tablaos más icónicos de la capital de España
articles.summary: La intérprete colombiana estuvo en uno de los tablaos más icónicos de la capital de España
articles.body: Shakira continúa con su puesta de largo en la ciudad de Madrid con sus 12 conciertos de la gira ‘Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour’ en su Estadio Shakira, en Villaverde. La intérprete actuó el 18, 19, 20, 25, 26 y 27 de septiembre y seguirá adelante con los shows los próximos 2, 3, 4, 9, 10 y 11 de octubre. Más allá de sus conciertos, la cantante colombiana también ha tenido tiempo libre para estar por algunos rincones de la capital de España. Este lunes, 28 de septiembre, la intérprete compartió en sus redes sociales cómo fue este día de desconexión en Madrid, lo que hizo y lo que consumió, ya que pidió un vino de 200 años para catar que le acabó por sorprender. Shakira escogió el Corral de La Morería, un tablao para vivir en primera persona el flamenco y que está ubicado junto al Palacio Real y con una trayectoria que se remonta a 1956. La cantante subió a sus historias de Instagram lo siguiente: “Solo la cultura puede salvarnos”. “En esta era de la mentira digital, esto es pura verdad. Este espectáculo tan emocionante ha tocado todas mis fibras, recordándome cuánto necesitamos el arte para hacernos más humanos”, añadía. Además, a la hora de cenar en el mencionado local, cató un vino de 200 años de antigüedad con una pipeta, según relató la intérprete en otra de sus historias de la red social de Meta: "Una sola gota voy a beber de la pipeta, porque una sola gota es toda una explosión de sabor”. Tras probarlo, su rostro fue de pura ensoñación: “No sé si merezco beber este vino tan preciado. Increíble, muchas gracias", sentenció.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson Is a New Kind of Movie Star: The Anti-Tom Cruise
articles.summary: In the last few years (ever since “Top Gun: Maverick”), Tom Cruise has often been hailed as The Last Movie Star. He’s certainly the gold standard, though it...
articles.body:
In the last few years (ever since "Top Gun: Maverick"), Tom Cruise has often been hailed as The Last Movie Star. He's certainly the gold standard, though it might be appropriate to add Brad Pitt and Julia Roberts to that category too. All three feel like The Last Movie Stars — though what I'm really saying, of course, is that they're the last movie stars to come out of the monoculture. That's why all three are monostars . You still feel that any of them, in the right light, can own the screen and own the world. That's baked into the karma of their presence. It's what drives their larger-than-life quality.

At the same time, it would be silly and backward to look at Tom and Brad and Julia and declare that the movie-star thing ends with them. Something ends with them. A certain kind of stardom. But that doesn't mean that the movie star has gone away. They're still being minted as we speak. Movie stars will probably never be as big as they used to be, but a new kind of star is rising from the ashes of our fragmented, niche-driven, post-romantic, postmodern world. And there is no more perfect an incarnation of the new stardom than Robert Pattinson.

Just watch him in "Primetime," where he plays Chris Hansen, the host of "To Catch a Predator," as a scoundrel and a sleaze, a man obsessed with ratings but also obsessed with seeing — and selling — himself as an arbiter of "virtue." The way Pattinson plays him, the Hansen of "Primetime" is like a come-hither fusion of Geraldo Rivera and Dracula; bathed in garish neon color, he looks even more like a vampire than Pattinson's Edward Cullen did; he practically has fangs. You might say, "Chris Hansen doesn't look like that," but what's uncanny about "Primetime" is that Pattinson seems to be playing the inner Hansen, the anxious opportunistic reptile who turned "To Catch a Predator" into a depraved form of squirm theater. The show pretended to be "capturing" men who solicited sex with children, but its true agenda was to humiliate them in public. It was really a voyeuristic revenge fantasy. You don't have to put yourself in the position of "defending pedophiles" to say that there's something seriously wrong with that.

Pattinson gives a mesmerizing performance, and the most fascinating thing about it is that it's a star performance. The movie portrays Chris Hansen as a petty showboating hypocrite, yet the way it works is that we're keyed into him. He's the film's oily center of gravity. And maybe the only way that could succeed is with a movie star. But could you imagine Tom Cruise or Brad Pitt in a role like this one? In his long and varied career, Cruise has gone "dark" — never more brilliantly than in "Magnolia" (his greatest performance; he was robbed of the Oscar when Harvey Weinstein used his tricks to win it for Michael Caine for the godawful "Cider House Rules"). Cruise, in a cartoon way, also goes dark in "Digger," a film that's about to enter the marketplace with a splat . But in "Primetime," Pattison goes pitch-black. That's his nervy dyspeptic magnetism. He's a star for the age of entropy — for an era when everything is falling apart.

Pattinson, of course, was launched by what felt like a tail-end monoculture franchise: the "Twilight" films. He played Edward, the 108-year-old teenage vampire, with a scowling leer that let you know this bloodsucker was no lost boy. But having established himself as a new-style neurasthenic matinee idol, Pattinson made a career decision that was driven and daring and eccentric, and he stuck to it. In 2012, the year of the concluding "Twilight" film, "Breaking Dawn — Part 2," he also starred in David Cronenberg's "Cosmopolis," playing a billionaire rotter who spends the entire movie riding around in a stretch limo, doing decadent things, and from that moment Pattinson never went back to "normal" roles.

He sought out the edgiest indies he could find, playing a neurotic T.E. Lawrence in Werner Herzog's "Queen of the Desert," a scuzzy Queens bank robber in the Safdie brothers' "Good Time," an explorer's recessive aide-de-camp in James Gray's "The Lost City of Z," and a surly drifter in Robert Eggers' "The Lighthouse," disappearing into every role with wormy devotion. During this period, which lasted close to 10 years, you practically expected to see Pattinson with a goth tattoo on his chest that read "Character Actor in Leading Man's Body."

He wasn't playing; he meant it. Even when his scuzz-indie streak finally ended, it wasn't in the usual way, with some big slick sellout. He did "Tenet" for Christopher Nolan, and then he finally took a leap into the franchise arena with "The Batman," which might be the most soul-jangling superhero movie ever made (its only competition would be "The Dark Knight," and in certain ways "The Batman" had it beat). His Bruce Wayne was brooding enough to make Christian Bale's look breezy. But the performance was moody and brilliant, and it crystalized Pattinson's cred. He was a character actor in a leading man's body. But he was something else too: a new kind of movie star. And in 2026, a year that Pattison owns, he drew on that anti-wholesome charisma in three performances, each one darker than the last: his nervous wreck of an impending groom in "The Drama"; his evil suitor in "The Odyssey" (a performance that could get him an Oscar); and his debauched carny-barker-of-pervs "newsman" in "Primetime."

It's not just that he's terrific in each of those films. In "The Drama" and "Primetime," he did that singular and defining movie-star thing: He put butts in seats . (He probably didn't hurt in that department in "The Odyssey" either.) It helped that he had A24 — the new Miramax — to help shepherd his popularity. But you can't shepherd what doesn't already exist. An entire generation has followed Pattinson from the "Twilight" movies to the moment he's in now.

To return, for a moment, to the old kind of star: Tom Cruise, Brad Pitt, and Julia Roberts are great actors, but in each case they won our hearts by playing idealized versions of who we are. Cruise the cocky clean maverick, Pitt the glam bad boy, Roberts the incandescent pretty woman: Their stardom is built on their being old-school movie gods. We already know how Cruise, after the flameout of "Digger," will pick himself up and dust himself off: He'll go back to playing the eternal star of our Tom Cruise dreams. But Robert Pattinson is the anti-Cruise, because his stardom is based on how far he's willing to stray from the ideal. That's his upside-down glamour — that we'll follow him anywhere.

articles.title: Aaron Sorkin reveals why Trump is unmentioned in 'Social Reckoning' movie
articles.summary: Director Aaron Sorkin revealed why President Donald Trump's name was deliberately cut from "The Social Reckoning," his new film exploring Facebook's role in polarization.
articles.body: Writer-director Aaron Sorkin explained why President Donald Trump’s name is omitted from his upcoming film examining Facebook’s influence on political discourse, including in the lead-up to the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol riot. When asked by Politico why Trump is not mentioned, Sorkin said he believed the president’s inclusion would become an unwelcome "distraction," adding that it was his decision to keep his name out of the film and that he wanted "clean hands." "I felt like as soon as we got to that scene, as soon as you saw anything ‘Trump,’ it would just become about something else," Sorkin told the outlet. "Again, I realize it’s going to kind of become about that ‘something else’ anyway. But I just like to have clean hands." 'THE SOCIAL RECKONING' TRAILER DROPS WITH JEREMY STRONG AS ZUCKERBERG IN AARON SORKIN'S FACEBOOK SEQUEL "The Social Reckoning," set to premiere in theaters Oct. 9, 2026, is a companion piece to Sorkin’s 2010 film "The Social Network," which chronicled the rise of Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg. The new movie follows whistleblower Frances Haugen, who provided internal Facebook documents to The Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz, which became the basis for the outlet's "Facebook Files" series examining the company's internal research and practices. The documents, published as part of a 2021 investigative series for the Journal, included internal research and findings about political polarization and the effects of Instagram on some young users' mental health. Sorkin acknowledged that the film is "political" but argued that it is "not a red-blue thing." BIPARTISAN LAWMAKERS WANT TO STRIP BIG TECH'S LEGAL IMMUNITY THAT CAN SHIELD SOCIAL MEDIA COMPANIES He said he wasn't directed to remove Trump's name from the movie but instead kept him out of it to keep Facebook at the center of the discussion. "I’m not going to deny, of course, that the movie is political. I just think it shouldn’t be. There’s really no reason for it to be," the screenwriter said. "I delivered the script and I think the next day I was in Tom Rothman’s office, and unsolicited, I told him that in that sequence we wouldn’t see any Trump signage at all. We won’t even see red hats. We’re going to see "Don’t Tread on Me," "Stop the Steal." You see American flags, Confederate flags, but it won’t be about MAGA versus everybody else, or even red-blue. It’s just going to be about Facebook’s role in the rise of divisiveness, extremism, and hyperpartisanship. So it was my choice. " A spokesperson for Meta said in 2022 that the platform was not responsible for violence on Jan. 6, instead pointing to Trump and others who promoted false claims that the 2020 election had been stolen. EX-NYPD INSPECTOR WARNS SOCIAL MEDIA LIKELY HELPED POLITICAL VIOLENCE ‘METASTASIZE’ INTO WHCD SCARE The film arrives as technology companies face continued scrutiny over social media’s harmful effects and as artificial intelligence draws attention in Washington. Social media’s influence has grown considerably in the 16 years since "The Social Network" was released and "The Social Reckoning" returns to Facebook to examine allegations about the platform’s role in amplifying political division and extremist content. Sorkin said he had considered revisiting Facebook whenever the company was in the news, but the story involving Haugen and Horwitz finally felt like a solid basis for a film. "The fact that the film has coincided with what tech people would call an inflection point is just happenstance," he said as his movie arrives to a more tech-skeptical audience in 2026. FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION "The Social Reckoning" is set to be released Oct. 9, roughly one month before the 2026 midterm elections. Sorkin told Politico that the upcoming elections played a part in deciding when the film would be released. "I don’t think this movie can change the course of electoral history," the filmmaker explained. "But these midterms are why I didn’t want to wait a year to make the movie. I didn’t want the movie to come out after the midterms because I didn’t think we’d be in the mood for it anymore." "And yeah, I thought maybe one little reminder might be helpful," he added. An insider close to the White House panned the movie as "delusional fiction." "Trump-deranged Democrats like Sorkin live in a political bubble that pathetically now encapsulates their art," they told Fox News Digital. "Judging by the trailers released, this delusional fiction looks so bad, it may even have the opposite effect of what was intended. What a loser!" articles.title: US Department of Education data reveals 1,100 sexual assault allegations against public school staff
articles.summary: Roughly 1,100 allegations of rape or sexual assault were made against public school employees in 2023-24, with 320 staff members resigning first.
articles.body: The U.S. Department of Education released new data showing that approximately 1,100 allegations of rape, attempted rape or sexual assault were made against public school employees during the 2023-24 school year. The revelations come amid the department's ongoing efforts to protect women and children, with a focus on enforcing Title IX across the country. The figures were included in the department’s latest Civil Rights Data Collection, a mandatory survey covering more than 17,000 public school districts and 97,000 schools nationwide. Of the roughly 1,100 allegations against staff members, approximately 320 resulted in an employee resigning or retiring before any final disciplinary action or termination, according to the report. About 280 resulted in findings that the employee was not responsible, 230 remained pending and 200 resulted in findings of responsibility. Approximately 90 led to duty reassignment before final disciplinary action or termination. FORMER NEW JERSEY MIDDLE SCHOOL TEACHER INDICTED ON NEW CHARGES INCLUDING MANUFACTURING CHILD ABUSE MATERIAL "Parents deserve to know that when they send their children to school, their safety comes first," Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights Kim Richey said in a statement. "The Civil Rights Data Collection gives us critical information to identify potential failures to protect students and hold school districts accountable when concerns arise," Richey continued. "Thanks to President Trump and Secretary McMahon’s leadership, the Office for Civil Rights will continue to follow the facts, enforce federal civil rights laws, and ensure schools take their responsibility to protect students seriously." School districts separately reported approximately 11,800 incidents of rape, attempted rape or other sexual assault during the 2023-24 school year. About 460, or roughly 4%, were reported as having been committed by school staff. EDUCATION DEPARTMENT RESCINDS BIDEN TITLE IX RULE, RESTORES TRUMP-ERA REGULATIONS The department cautioned that the number of reported incidents and the number of allegations against staff are separate measurements. It also said reporting in this area is still developing. The staff sexual-offense questions were first included as optional elements in the 2020-21 collection and became mandatory for 2023-24. The findings come after the department’s Office for Civil Rights launched a national K-12 initiative in July aimed at protecting students from sexual misconduct by adults in schools. The initiative included 20 directed investigations of districts that the department said appeared to have inadequately addressed staff-on-student sexual misconduct. ed.gov CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The department said schools that fail to respond appropriately to sexual harassment or abuse may violate Title IX and could face enforcement action, including the potential loss of federal funding. Trump's Department of Education, under McMahon's leadership, has made the protection of women and children a focus. The department announced at the beginning of Trump’s second term that it would enforce the 2020 Title IX regulations after a federal court vacated the Biden administration’s 2024 rewrite. On Monday, the department formally removed the vacated Biden-era rule from the Code of Federal Regulations and restored the earlier regulatory language. The 2020 regulations establish requirements for how federally funded schools must respond to allegations of sexual harassment and assault while providing due-process protections for accused students. The administration has also directed federal agencies to interpret sex-based protections according to biological sex rather than gender identity. Trump’s January 2025 executive order defines "woman" as an adult human female and "girl" as a juvenile human female, while defining sex as an immutable biological classification. The Education Department subsequently instructed its Office for Civil Rights to enforce Title IX consistent with those definitions. That approach has guided the department’s enforcement efforts involving women’s sports, sex-separated facilities and schools’ responses to sexual misconduct. Title IX prohibits sex discrimination in education programs and activities receiving federal funding, and institutions found in violation can ultimately risk losing that assistance if they refuse to comply. The administration has also made preserving women’s sports a central part of its Title IX agenda. Trump signed an executive order in February 2025 directing federal agencies to oppose male participation in women’s athletic competition, while the Education Department has opened investigations and pursued enforcement actions against schools and athletic organizations whose policies it says deny female athletes equal opportunities, privacy or safety.
